name: Monumental Earthworks of Poverty Point
description: In northeastern Louisiana, hunter-fisher-gatherers built a vast earthen complex about 3,700 to 3,100 years ago. Six curved, concentric ridges surround a central plaza, with five mounds nearby. Nothing in North America matched this scale of earthmoving for at least 2,000 years. Visitors can walk the ridges and climb the mounds.
